key_insight: In controlled wake flows, POD produces smoother latent dynamics that are easier to forecast long-term, while CAEs compress better but are more prone to unstable or divergent predictions.
engineering_relevance: For real-time flow control, predictive stability can matter more than maximum compression when building hardware-feasible reduced-order models for MPC or reinforcement learning.
method: Compare POD, convolutional autoencoders, and variational autoencoders as spatial encoders.
Use LSTM-based temporal predictors in latent space.
Test on two actuated 2D wakes: a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball.
evidence_signal: Across the two controlled wake datasets, CAEs gave sharper short-term reconstructions but the abstract reports faster degradation and higher catastrophic-divergence risk in long-horizon forecasts than POD-based models.
watch_item: Higher compression does not guarantee usable control forecasts; latent-dynamics irregularity and divergence risk should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
